data.name: Keep Defending
data.detailed_description:
Keep Defending is a first-person VR tower defense archery game where you build up your defenses during the enemy onslaught.

Target enemies before they reach your gate and earn gold to set up ever more capable defenses including crossbows, fireball-shooting wizards, brave knights, cannons, and more as you try and deal with the approaching hordes in a variety of different environments and scenarios.



Features

  • A host of enemies from Barbarian hordes to Skeleton armies and greater (much greater) dangers.
  • A range of defenses for you to employ during play to ensure the enemies don't get through.
  • Different scenarios to test your defensive tactics from small villages to large castles, frozen wastes, underground caves, and beyond.
  • Ambush scenarios where you must destroy the enemy before they escape the lethal range of your attackers.
  • Advance scenarios where you progress through different zones and build up your defenses for a grand finale!
  • Weather conditions and time of day effects offer additional gameplay challenges.
  • Beware boss enemies that destroy your defenses with a single hit.
  • Precision scoring - earn higher scores the further away targets are hit.
  • Steam leaderboards, stats, and achievements.
  • Support for HTC Vive, Oculus Rift (with Touch controllers), and Windows Mixed Reality headsets.

reviews.review:
Keep Defending takes the familiar structure of tower defense and turns it into a much more hands-on virtual reality experience. Instead of watching enemies march toward carefully positioned defenses from an overhead viewpoint, the player stands directly on the battlefield and contributes to the fight with a bow. Developed and published by Faster Time Games, the game combines VR archery, defensive unit placement, resource management, and escalating enemy waves into a compact action-strategy experience. The concept is simple to understand, but the physical involvement of aiming and firing arrows gives it a distinctive personality compared with conventional tower defense games.

The basic objective revolves around preventing waves of enemies from overwhelming the position under your protection. Archery forms the foundation of combat, requiring players to physically aim and fire at approaching targets. Eliminating enemies rewards gold, which can then be spent on additional defenses. This creates a satisfying relationship between personal combat performance and strategic development. Accurate shooting provides the resources necessary to strengthen the battlefield, while well-positioned defenses reduce the number of threats that must be handled personally.

Several defensive options broaden the tactical possibilities. Crossbows can provide additional ranged attacks, knights contribute direct defensive support, wizards bring magical assistance, and cannons offer heavier firepower. Deciding where resources should be spent becomes increasingly important as enemy waves become more demanding. Investing heavily in one location may produce a powerful defensive position while leaving another route vulnerable. The strategic systems are not exceptionally complicated, but they provide enough decision-making to prevent the experience from becoming nothing more than a VR archery shooting gallery.

Accuracy is encouraged through a scoring system that rewards more impressive shots. Long-range attacks can produce higher scores, giving confident archers an incentive to engage enemies before they reach comfortable shooting distance. This risk-and-reward approach adds a welcome skill component because simply surviving is not necessarily the only objective. Players interested in competitive performance can attempt to improve their scores and compare their results through leaderboards. Statistics and achievements provide additional reasons to revisit completed scenarios and refine previous performances.

Enemy variety contributes to the increasing pressure. Players encounter hostile forces ranging from barbarians and skeletons to larger fantasy creatures and dangerous bosses. Particularly threatening opponents can quickly damage or destroy valuable defensive assets, meaning target prioritization becomes important. A player who concentrates exclusively on the easiest enemies may suddenly discover that a more dangerous attacker has broken through and eliminated an important defensive position. These moments make the player balance immediate threats against enemies that could create larger problems if ignored.

The selection of environments helps keep the campaign visually varied. Defensive battles can take place around villages and castles as well as frozen landscapes, caves, and other fantasy settings. Changes in terrain, atmosphere, weather, and time of day prevent every encounter from looking identical. The graphics are relatively straightforward by modern VR standards, but the visual design generally prioritizes readability. Being able to identify approaching enemies and judge distances matters significantly when firing arrows across large areas.

Scenario variation is one of the game's more useful features. Standard defensive encounters are supplemented by modes that alter the usual objectives. Ambush situations can require enemies to be eliminated before they escape effective attack range, while advancing scenarios involve moving through different zones and developing defenses along the way. These variations prevent the campaign from relying exclusively on stationary wave defense. They also encourage players to reconsider strategies that may have worked perfectly in previous levels.

Keep Defending is at its strongest when the direct VR action and automated defensive systems operate together. During the opening portions of an encounter, the player's bow may carry much of the workload. As gold accumulates and more units are deployed, the battlefield gradually becomes busier and more capable of fighting independently. Watching a defensive network grow from a relatively vulnerable position into a coordinated collection of ranged weapons, warriors, magic, and artillery provides a satisfying sense of progression within individual scenarios.

There are limitations to the formula. The strategic component is accessible rather than deeply sophisticated, so players expecting the complexity of dedicated tower defense games may find the available management relatively modest. Likewise, the repeated cycle of shooting enemies, collecting resources, placing defenses, and surviving increasingly difficult waves can eventually become repetitive. Much of the long-term appeal depends on whether the player enjoys VR archery enough to replay scenarios for better scores and improved efficiency.

The VR requirement is especially important. Keep Defending was built around tracked virtual reality controls and physical archery interaction rather than traditional keyboard, mouse, or controller gameplay. Standing and room-scale VR suit the design well, but this also substantially narrows the audience. It is best approached as a dedicated PC VR title rather than a traditional tower defense game that happens to include optional VR support.

Steam Deck compatibility is therefore poor for practical purposes. The game is VR-only and depends on hardware and motion controls that the Steam Deck does not provide as a self-contained handheld system. Even if compatibility layers could technically launch parts of the software, the built-in Deck controls cannot reproduce the intended tracked VR archery experience. Players looking specifically for portable Steam Deck gameplay should consider it unsuitable, while those using a proper PC VR configuration are the intended audience.

Overall, Keep Defending offers an enjoyable interpretation of tower defense by placing the player directly inside the action. Its combination of physical archery, gold management, defensive deployment, varied enemies, bosses, alternative scenarios, scoring, and environmental changes creates more tactical involvement than a basic VR shooting gallery. It may lack the depth of larger strategy games and shows the straightforward presentation associated with earlier PC VR releases, but the underlying combination of genres works surprisingly well. For VR players who enjoy archery and defensive strategy in roughly equal measure, it remains a focused and entertaining experience.

Rating: 7/10
